title: Wednesday briefing: Inside sweeping UK sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements
summary_or_snippet: In today's newsletter: Ed Miliband has announced the strongest statement on Israel's actions ever issued by the the UK government, but will it make a meaningful difference to Palestinians? Good morning. For almost half a century, British governments have condemned illegal Israeli settlements, acknowledging they represent an obstacle to peace and threaten the prospect of a two-state solution. And yet no government has ever compelled Israel to stop its expansion. Ed Miliband's statement in the House of Commons yesterday was an attempt to change that. In a powerful and emotive speech, the foreign secretary recounted childhood memories of picking oranges on his grandmother's kibbutz, accused Israeli "terrorists" of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and announced a series of new measures intended to address what he described as a "deeply painful contrast" between rhetoric and reality. UK news | Police have been told by the government they expect better intelligence gathering after masked far-right groups took to the streets at the weekend, the Guardian has learned, as the Kent force admitted mishandling warnings of potential trouble. UK politics | Andy Burnham should tackle inequality in the UK by introducing a wealth tax, universal free personal social care and bringing gas and electricity networks under public ownership, according to a report from more than a dozen influential thinkers. Airline industry | Flight delays and cancellations were expected to continue today at UK airports after another air traffic control failure kept planes grounded for hours, affecting hundreds of thousands of passengers. Iran | Iranian forces claimed to have seized an American underwater drone in the strait of Hormuz that the US military said had "malfunctioned" more than a day earlier. US news | Donald Trump gave sizeable holiday gifts to four White House aides, according to new financial disclosures released by the administration, including $45,000 to executive assistant Natalie Harp.

title: UK accuses Israeli 'terrorists' of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said he would "not stand by" as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act , "fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel". An import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories and a new ban for arms licences and other exports that "materially contribute to the occupation". title: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions announced
summary_or_snippet: Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem in response to sweeping UK sanctions on goods from illegal settlements. Reacting to Ed Miliband's description of violent Jewish settler activity on the occupied Palestinian West Bank as "ethnic cleansing" carried out with the tacit backing of the Netanyahu government , Israel's foreign minister, Gideon Sa'ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several UK MPs.
